slot.brief: Figure with concentration-vs-time or ln[A] vs time plots for first-order reactions; extract rate constant from slope or compare two reactants' half-lives.

stem: Two first-order reactions, $X$ and $Y$, have the $\ln([C]/[C]_0)$ versus time plots shown in the figure. When $[Y]=[Y]_0/4$, what fraction of its initial concentration remains for $X$?

verdicts.working: From the graph at 10 min, ln([Y]/[Y]₀) = −1 and ln([X]/[X]₀) = −2, so X’s decay rate is twice Y’s. Thus when Y/Y₀ = 1/4, X/X₀ = (1/4)² = 1/16.

working:
$k_X=2/10=0.20\ \text{min}^{-1}$; $k_Y=1/10=0.10\ \text{min}^{-1}$; $[Y]/[Y]_0=1/4\Rightarrow t=\ln 4/0.10$; $[X]/[X]_0=e^{-0.20t}=e^{-2\ln4}=1/16$.

Independent check: From the graph at 10 min, ln([Y]/[Y]₀) = −1 and ln([X]/[X]₀) = −2, so X’s decay rate is twice Y’s. Thus when Y/Y₀ = 1/4, X/X₀ = (1/4)² = 1/16.

draft.stem: Two first-order reactions, $X$ and $Y$, have the $\ln([C]/[C]_0)$ versus time plots shown in the figure. When $[Y]=[Y]_0/4$, what fraction of its initial concentration remains for $X$?

figure.description: Draw a Cartesian graph with horizontal axis $t$ (min), ticks at 0, 5 and 10, and vertical axis $\ln([C]/[C]_0)$, ticks at 0, $-1$ and $-2$. Plot two straight lines beginning at $(0,0)$. The line labelled X passes through $(10,-2)$; the line labelled Y passes through $(10,-1)$. Label both lines clearly.

draft.distractor_notes: A: doubles the exponent; C: uses only one factor of the rate-constant ratio; D: reports the fraction for Y.
